thesis: Dell reported fiscal Q2 2027 on September 1, the day of this run: record revenue of $47 billion against a $44.92 billion consensus and adjusted EPS of $7.04 against $4.91 expected, with the annual outlook raised for the second time this year — FY2027 revenue to $192 billion (a $25 billion increase) and adjusted EPS to $25.50 from $17.90 — alongside a $74 billion AI-server revenue forecast and Q3 guidance of $49 billion revenue and $6.50 adjusted EPS, both above consensus. Shares rose about 6% in extended trading, and today's 2.09x volume spike against the prior 30 bars is that print. The strongest counter-case is the one flagged going into the quarter: that the AI memory bill would finally reach server gross margin. That does not change the read here, because the company answered it directly in the same disclosure — an EPS outlook lifted from $17.90 to $25.50 is not consistent with margin compression being absorbed quietly, and the raise is company guidance rather than analyst inference. This suggests the position continues to be supported.
invalidation: Dell walks back the raised FY2027 adjusted EPS outlook, or discloses AI-server gross margin compression at the Q3 report

thesis: Microsoft's fiscal Q4 2026 report on July 29 is a confirmed, company-disclosed catalyst: adjusted EPS of $4.74 against $4.24 expected on revenue of $90.01 billion, Azure revenue passing $100 billion for the full fiscal year (up 41%), and Q4 Azure growth accelerating to 43% year over year, with record commercial RPO reported alongside. The strongest counter-case is that the acceleration is being bought with heavy AI infrastructure spending and that the roughly 30% move in the shares since late July has already discounted it. That does not change the read, because the acceleration and the record contracted backlog are disclosed evidence that the spending is converting into booked revenue rather than being announced ahead of it — the growth rate rose rather than held while the spend was underway. No capital expenditure figure is asserted here: the sources read this run did not state one.
invalidation: Azure growth decelerates back toward the high-30s at the FQ1 report, or commercial RPO stops growing sequentially

thesis: Nvidia's fiscal Q2 2027 report on August 26 is a confirmed, company-disclosed catalyst: results surpassed analyst forecasts and guidance came in above estimates, and the shares rose 8.7% on the print. Disclosed alongside it, Amazon Web Services agreed to buy 2 million Nvidia GPUs and adopt the new Vera CPU — a named customer commitment rather than a projection. The strongest counter-case available from this run's research is the late-August rotation out of high-growth chip names after hawkish Federal Reserve commentary at Jackson Hole, which carried NVDA from a 227.98 close on August 27 back to 217.44 on September 1. That is a rates-driven move across the whole group, not anything disclosed about Nvidia's demand, and the AWS commitment is company-specific and unaffected by it. The 70% FY2028 revenue growth figure circulating in coverage is an analyst projection against a 44% LSEG-surveyed consensus, not company guidance, and is treated as such. This suggests the position continues to be supported.
invalidation: A named hyperscaler publicly defers or trims announced GPU orders, or Nvidia guides below consensus at the next report

thesis: Lumentum's fiscal Q4 report on August 12 is a confirmed, company-disclosed beat and raise: revenue of $1.01 billion against a $987.7 million estimate, adjusted EPS of $3.23 more than doubling year over year, and Q1 guidance above expectations. The shares gapped about 8% pre-market and closed up roughly 14% on the day, and Mizuho, JPMorgan, Raymond James, Citi and BNP Paribas raised targets afterwards. The strongest counter-case is that the entire AI-optics complex de-rated in the same window — Coherent fell 12.75% on August 18 and Corning guided its September quarter below an elevated consensus after its own beat — which would imply a sector-wide demand-expectation reset that Lumentum cannot escape. That does not change the read, for a concrete reason: Lumentum's print and guide landed inside that de-rating window, both came in above consensus, and the stock held its gain through the peer selloff rather than giving it back — the reset visible in peer expectations was not corroborated by Lumentum's own disclosed numbers. The 60-day window shows the stock up 18.8% while its optical peers fell. Analyst price targets are opinion and are not part of this read.
invalidation: Lumentum guides the December quarter below consensus, or an 800G/1.6T customer publicly defers orders

thesis: Corcept has a confirmed, completed regulatory approval: the FDA approved relacorilant (Lifyorli) in combination with nab-paclitaxel for adults with platinum-resistant epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer, completed roughly 2.5 months ahead of the goal date, and the company guides 2026 revenue of $950 million to $1.05 billion, above 30% year-over-year growth. The counter-case is named and it is not settled: the separate Cushing's syndrome NDA for the same molecule drew a Complete Response Letter, and Corcept has resubmitted with an expected six-month review, so an unresolved binary regulatory outcome sits ahead on a date this run's research did not establish. That pending decision is a regulatory review, not a lawsuit or an investigation, so no active_litigation flag is raised. The 23.8% 60-day advance and the stock sitting 10.4% below its 52-week high reflect the approval and the run before it, not the pending Cushing's decision. This suggests a constructive read with the pending binary keeping conviction below the top tier.
invalidation: The resubmitted Cushing's NDA draws a second Complete Response Letter, or 2026 revenue guidance is cut below the $950 million floor

thesis: Astera Labs' Q2 2026 report on August 4 was company-disclosed and positive: record results beating on revenue and earnings with 104% year-over-year revenue growth, Q3 guidance of $540-560 million (roughly 40% sequential growth at the midpoint), and management projecting non-GAAP EPS of $1.16-$1.21. The shares nevertheless fell about 12% on the print and are down 35.3% across the 60-day window (close_60d_ago 432.74 to latest_close 279.91). The explanation available from this run's research is largely mechanical — profit-taking after a four-session pre-earnings rally, with coverage stating outright that the results are not what moved the stock, plus the broader August de-rating of AI-hardware names; higher operating expenses from continued product-roadmap investment were the one disclosed drag. Because the adverse move is explained by positioning rather than by anything disclosed about the business, the counter-case is engaged but unresolved. This suggests the disclosed fundamentals still support holding, but only at low conviction.
invalidation: Q3 revenue lands below the guided $540-560 million range, or Astera guides Q4 sequentially flat or down

thesis: AMD's disclosed fundamentals remain strong — data center revenue rose 107% last quarter and the first gigawatt of Instinct MI450 capacity for OpenAI is scheduled to begin deploying in the second half of this year — but the 16.7% 60-day decline is explained in this run's sources as sector- and macro-driven rather than company-specific: a 6.7% drop as investors took profits after AMD's AI event, and a 2.33% fall alongside Nvidia and Intel on hawkish Federal Reserve commentary from Jackson Hole. A macro/sector-wide driver and a positioning-driven move both cap this read. Coverage also notes OpenAI can purchase up to 160 million AMD shares, about $73 billion at late-August prices; the sources read here did not state when that arrangement was disclosed, so the dilution flag is applied conservatively rather than on a confirmed date, and no figure beyond what those sources state is asserted. Reports that MI450-series chips are behind schedule are described in coverage as rumours and are not treated as fact here. This suggests a long only at low conviction.
invalidation: AMD confirms an MI450 schedule slip, or data center revenue growth decelerates materially at the next report

thesis: Applied Optoelectronics posted a confirmed, company-disclosed Q2 2026 on August 6: EPS of $0.06 against $0.01 expected and revenue of $191.9 million, up 86% year over year and a fifth consecutive record quarter driven by AI datacenter optics and CATV, with Q3 guidance of $255-290 million revenue and $0.11-$0.26 adjusted EPS as 800G and 1.6T products ramp. Against that, the company unveiled a further $600 million at-the-market equity offering and the shares fell about 10% after hours on it; the stock is 55.9% below its 52-week high and down 16.2% over the 60-day window. The dilution is a disclosed, quantified cost set against disclosed, accelerating growth rather than an offsetting unknown, but an active ATM program is itself a risk flag and holds this read at low conviction. This suggests a long only at low conviction.
invalidation: Q3 revenue lands below the guided $255 million floor, or a further equity raise is announced before the current ATM is drawn down

thesis: Rocket Lab's evidence this run is offsetting rather than net-positive. Company-disclosed on the positive side: roughly $663 million in US Space Force awards across eight days in late July, including a record $266 million launch deal and a $397 million award to build threat-tracking satellites to fly on Neutron. Against that, the Q2 loss was $0.08 per share versus a $0.06 FactSet estimate — a miss — and the shares fell 19.4% over seven sessions into late August while the S&P 500 held, which coverage reads as a repricing of what investors will pay for growth that still burns cash; Form 144 filings from the Chief Operations Officer (35,558 shares, about $2.35 million) and a separate $22 million founder filing landed in the same stretch. The 60-day move is -32.8%. The awards are real and the profitability concern is real, and neither resolves the other until Neutron flies. This suggests standing aside rather than entering.
invalidation: Neutron completes a successful first flight, or Rocket Lab reports a quarter with positive operating cash flow

thesis: AST SpaceMobile's 30.8% 60-day decline is explained in this run's research as macro rather than company-specific: the shares fell 15.5% intraday on August 28 after Fed Chair Kevin Warsh signalled inflation is now the Fed's focus and raised the odds of a rate hike, with coverage tying the sensitivity directly to AST building its satellite constellation largely on borrowed money, so higher rates raise borrowing costs and change the arithmetic of the build. Deutsche Bank cut its target to $93 from $106 and Piper Sandler to $98 from $100 during the month; those are analyst opinions, not disclosure, and carry no weight here. No company-disclosed catalyst — positive or negative — surfaced in this run's research, so the entire move rests on a sector- and rate-driven driver against a capital-intensive, debt-funded balance sheet. This suggests avoiding an entry.
invalidation: AST discloses funded, non-dilutive financing for the constellation, or the shares re-rate on company disclosure rather than rate expectations

thesis: Intel's 27.2% 60-day decline rests on disclosed structural facts rather than sentiment. Intel Foundry posted a $2.8 billion operating loss in Q2 2026, and coverage estimates that at the current rate the division consumes more than $10 billion of operating losses through the end of 2027 before reaching the scale needed to approach profitability. The company raised roughly $20 billion of equity priced at $95 to fund a capital programme of about the same size in 2026, and the shares closed August below that offer price at $89.47 on August 31 — the market is declining to fund the plan at the price at which it was sold — while reported CPU market share sits at a three-decade low. The strongest counter-case available is the CEO's own share purchase alongside Intel's AI-related growth; that does not change the read, because a single insider purchase does not offset a loss trajectory of that size, and the dilution is completed rather than prospective, so it is already in the share count. This suggests avoiding an entry.
invalidation: Intel discloses a large external foundry commitment with named volume, or foundry operating losses narrow materially at the next report

thesis: Corning's read is mixed on the company's own reporting, and both sides are quoted here. Q2 2026 on July 28 beat Wall Street estimates on both revenue and earnings, while third-quarter revenue guidance came in below an elevated consensus; CNBC reported the shares fell about 12% on the print, dragging optical peers with them. Optical Communications growth decelerated from 36% in Q1 to 32% in Q2 — still growth, but slowing. August added a Wall Street Zen downgrade to Hold on August 24, following earlier target cuts from Barclays and J.P. Morgan and a Negative Catalyst Watch; those are analyst opinions, not disclosure. One source described the post-earnings drop as more than 20% against CNBC's 12%; the CNBC figure is used and the discrepancy is left explicitly unresolved rather than reconciled by inference. A beat paired with a guide-down is offsetting evidence that this run cannot net out. This suggests avoiding an entry.
invalidation: Corning guides the December quarter above consensus, or Optical Communications growth re-accelerates above the 36% Q1 rate

thesis: Coherent's fiscal Q4 on August 12 was strong on the disclosed numbers — adjusted EPS of $1.74 on $2.04 billion of revenue, datacenter and communications revenue up 59% year over year, Q1 guidance of as much as $2.4 billion, and co-packaged optics shipping in the second half of 2026 — and the shares fell anyway: about 4.4% on the print, 12.75% on August 18 in a sector-wide AI-optics selloff, and 6.19% on August 19, for a 19.0% decline across the 60-day window. The counter-case is specific and unsettled: inventory rose 79.5% to $2.58 billion and receivables 39.3% against $1.1 billion of capital spending, with coverage framing the cash burn from the AI-optics expansion as outpacing cash generation. Strong disclosed growth and a deteriorating working-capital picture point in opposite directions and this run's research cannot net them out. This suggests standing aside.
invalidation: Inventory and receivables growth decelerate below revenue growth at the next report, or Coherent guides the following quarter below consensus

thesis: Marvell's fiscal Q2 2027 was a company-disclosed beat and raise: record revenue of $2.739 billion, up 37% year over year, adjusted EPS of $0.94, both ahead of guidance, with the FY27 revenue outlook raised by $500 million and FY28 by $1.5 billion, and next-quarter guidance of $2.0-2.2 billion revenue and $0.69-$0.79 EPS against a $0.66 consensus. The shares fell about 14% regardless, with coverage attributing it to doubts that Marvell's large Google custom-silicon agreement contributes meaningfully before fiscal 2029. The raise does cover FY27 and FY28, which partly answers the timing objection — but it does not explain why the market discounted a beat and a raise by 14%, and this run's research cannot establish which reading is right. A counter-case engaged and left unsettled is unresolved evidence, and a 14% adverse move against disclosed good news says the facts in hand are incomplete. This suggests avoiding an entry until the Google agreement's near-term contribution is quantified.
invalidation: Marvell names near-term revenue from the Google agreement, or custom-silicon revenue lands below the raised outlook at the next report

thesis: Sandisk's disclosed fiscal 2026 numbers are extraordinary — revenue up 175% year over year to $20.25 billion with datacenter revenue up 437% — and the August 13 investor day set long-term targets of double-digit revenue growth through 2030 and an 80% non-GAAP gross margin. The counter-case is the cycle itself and it is not settled: coverage estimates Sandisk rode a roughly 70% jump in NAND prices, while TrendForce projects 10% to 15% for the current quarter, a sharp deceleration in the input that produced those results. Reported long-term supply agreements are said to carry a floor near $0.29 per gigabyte, broadly in line with Q2 2026 average selling prices, which limits downside on price but does not restore the growth rate. With the shares at $1,532 against a $50.07 52-week low and still 34.9% below the 52-week high, a decelerating price cycle set against a vertical re-rating is offsetting evidence this run cannot resolve. This suggests avoiding an entry.
invalidation: NAND contract pricing turns negative quarter over quarter, or Sandisk guides datacenter revenue below the prior quarter

thesis: SpaceX's 11.3% 60-day decline has a mechanical explanation rather than a disclosed fundamental one. The company listed on June 12, 2026 and is working through a staggered lockup that releases roughly 88% of its 13 billion shares through 2027: about 911.5 million shares became tradable on August 6, which the stock absorbed while rising 6%, and roughly 319 million more from early employees and investors unlocked on August 22, after which the shares fell back toward the $135 IPO price. Coverage also cites a pushed-back Starship catch and China's LandSpace recovering an orbital-class booster on land as competitive headlines in the same stretch. Company news in the window was positive — a ten-year Starlink licence in the UAE, the Falcon Heavy launch of NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope on August 30, and a stated plan for a $100 billion Louisiana spaceport. Supply overhang is a mechanical driver, and the larger tranches are still ahead: about 1.3 billion shares around third-quarter results in early November, then the 180-day expiry in December. This suggests avoiding until that calendar clears.
invalidation: The November tranche unlocks without the shares breaking lower, or SpaceX discloses contracted revenue that moves the stock on fundamentals rather than float

thesis: Cerebras' Q2 2026 report on August 12 published two figures that point in opposite directions, and both are reported here. On GAAP revenue the company missed: $180 million against $194 million expected. On the company-preferred 'core revenue' measure, which strips out pass-through revenue and amortisation of customer warrant assets, revenue was $210 million, and the adjusted loss of $0.05 per share beat a $0.17 expectation. The net loss was $450.5 million, of which $386.6 million was stock compensation. Full-year core revenue guidance was raised to $880-890 million from $855-865 million, and the following quarter's core revenue was guided to $214-216 million. The shares fell about 14% in extended trading and now sit 7.3% above their 52-week low, with a staggered lockup adding share supply through this period. A GAAP miss against a raised non-GAAP outlook, and a 14% adverse reaction to it, is unresolved evidence rather than a clear net read. This suggests avoiding an entry.
invalidation: GAAP revenue converges toward core revenue at the next report, or Cerebras guides full-year core revenue below $880 million

thesis: LYTE is the Roundhill Photonics & Optics ETF, which began trading on August 6, 2026 at $25.73 with about $72 million of first-day volume; reported top holdings are Lumentum (15.42%), Coherent (15.23%), NewLink (14.59%), ZTE (14.22%) and Tianfu Communication (7.9%). It qualified here only on proximity to a 52-week low that is four weeks old — the fund's entire price history is 19 bars, and the script's volume baseline had to fall back to 18 days — so that extreme carries very little information. What moves it is the sector: the same AI-optics de-rating that hit Coherent and Corning through August, which is a sector-wide driver rather than a company-specific catalyst, and a fund publishes no disclosure of its own on which to build a thesis. This suggests avoiding an entry.
invalidation: The underlying optical names re-rate on their own disclosed results, which would make the fund's proximity to a launch-period low uninformative in either direction
